react_result.final_narrative_text: Three independent pathway-analysis paradigms converge on disrupted tyrosine metabolism as the dominant biological signal. RaMP multi-database ORA identified the ADHD and autism (ASD) pathway (WP:WP5420) as the top hit with FDR 7.4e-9 and fold-enrichment 177, driven by five input metabolites: L-tyrosine, dopamine, glycine, tyramine, and uric acid. Within the same ORA result, the KEGG:map00350 Tyrosine metabolism pathway reached FDR 1.6e-6 with a fold-enrichment of 336. The m/z-direct Mummichog method independently ranked Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism) first with p=0.00025, matching 10 of 10 pathway compounds including L-tyrosine, dopamine, tyramine, and dihydrobiopterin, the latter anchoring the tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) cofactor branch. Biopterin metabolism (MUMM:biopterin_metabolism) appeared as a secondary hit (p=0.0128), confirming BH4 biosynthesis involvement. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA independently confirmed hsa00350 Tyrosine metabolism at p=0.0006, with dopamine, L-tyrosine, and tyramine as the three overlapping compounds. The InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all input metabolites, ruling out namespace artefacts. Losartan, homogentisic acid, N-acetylgalactosamine, and iron were not detected in the tyrosine metabolism pathway by any tool, suggesting they may be bystander signals or reflect off-target drug metabolism. The convergent evidence implicates altered aromatic amino acid catabolism and monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis, consistent with neurological or psychiatric phenotypic readouts in the treatment group.

RaMP multi-database ORA identified the ADHD and autism (ASD) pathway (WP:WP5420) as the top hit with FDR 7.4e-9 and fold-enrichment 177, driven by five input metabolites: L-tyrosine, dopamine, glycine, tyramine, and uric acid. Within the same ORA result, the KEGG:map00350 Tyrosine metabolism pathway reached FDR 1.6e-6 with a fold-enrichment of 336. The m/z-direct Mummichog method independently ranked Tyrosine metabolism (MUMM:tyrosine_metabolism) first with p=0.00025, matching 10 of 10 pathway compounds including L-tyrosine, dopamine, tyramine, and dihydrobiopterin, the latter anchoring the tetrahydrobiopterin (BH4) cofactor branch. Biopterin metabolism (MUMM:biopterin_metabolism) appeared as a secondary hit (p=0.0128), confirming BH4 biosynthesis involvement. MetaboAnalystR KEGG-specific ORA independently confirmed hsa00350 Tyrosine metabolism at p=0.0006, with dopamine, L-tyrosine, and tyramine as the three overlapping compounds. The InChIKey reconciliation confirmed zero structural conflicts across all input metabolites, ruling out namespace artefacts. Losartan, homogentisic acid, N-acetylgalactosamine, and iron were not detected in the tyrosine metabolism pathway by any tool, suggesting they may be bystander signals or reflect off-target drug metabolism. The convergent evidence implicates altered aromatic amino acid catabolism and monoamine neurotransmitter biosynthesis, consistent with neurological or psychiatric phenotypic readouts in the treatment group.
